# windows_iis_app_pool (Resource)

Manages an IIS application pool on a remote Windows host via SSH and PowerShell (`WebAdministration` module: `New-WebAppPool`, `Get-ItemProperty` / `Set-ItemProperty IIS:\AppPools\<name>`, `Remove-WebAppPool`, `Start-WebAppPool` / `Stop-WebAppPool`).

Only the attributes configured in Terraform are written; every other setting on the host is left untouched and undiffed (unconfigured attributes reflect the observed value). The runtime `state` (`Started` / `Stopped`) is enforced only when configured.

A `SpecificUser` identity needs `identity_username` plus the WriteOnly `identity_password_wo`, which travels to the host on stdin and is never persisted in state; rotation is driven exclusively by `identity_password_wo_version`. After `terraform import` the password cannot be recovered: set it together with a fresh version before the next apply.

Requires IIS on the target host: install it with the `windows_feature` resource (`Web-Server`; add `Web-Mgmt-Console` / `Web-Scripting-Tools` for the `WebAdministration` module on Server Core).

**Partial failures:** if creation fails after the pool was already registered in IIS, the provider persists the observed state before reporting the error, so the resource is marked tainted. If update fails after IIS applied part of the change, the provider saves the observed partial state before reporting the error, restoring `identity_password_wo_version` from prior state so a failed rotation still diffs on retry. Fix the cause and run `terraform apply` again to reconcile.

A nil state on error does not guarantee nothing was created: a failure that returns no state leaves an orphaned pool that must be removed with `Remove-WebAppPool` or re-adopted with `terraform import`.

Import format: `<pool name>`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Manage an IIS application pool: no managed code, always running, recycled
# nightly at 03:00. Only the configured attributes are written
# (Set-ItemProperty); everything else on the host is left untouched.
#
# Requires IIS on the target host (WebAdministration module): install it
# with windows_feature first (Web-Server; add Web-Mgmt-Console /
# Web-Scripting-Tools for the module on Server Core).
resource "windows_feature" "iis" {
  name                     = "Web-Server"
  include_management_tools = true
}

resource "windows_iis_app_pool" "api" {
  name                    = "api"
  managed_runtime_version = "" # No Managed Code
  managed_pipeline_mode   = "Integrated"
  start_mode              = "AlwaysRunning"

  idle_timeout_minutes               = 0 # disabled
  recycling_periodic_restart_minutes = 0 # disabled
  recycling_schedule                 = ["03:00:00"]
  recycling_private_memory_kb        = 1048576
  rapid_fail_protection              = true

  state = "Started"

  depends_on = [windows_feature.iis]

  # Bound every remote operation explicitly. Without this block each operation
  # defaults to 10 minutes; a stalled PowerShell/SSH session then surfaces a
  # timeout diagnostic instead of blocking Terraform indefinitely.
  timeouts = {
    create = "10m"
    read   = "10m"
    update = "10m"
    delete = "10m"
  }
}

# A pool running as a domain service account. The password is WriteOnly: it
# travels to the host on stdin, is never persisted in state, and is re-sent
# only when identity_password_wo_version changes (bump the version to rotate).
resource "windows_iis_app_pool" "svc" {
  name                         = "svc"
  identity_type                = "SpecificUser"
  identity_username            = "CONTOSO\\svc-web"
  identity_password_wo         = var.svc_web_password
  identity_password_wo_version = 1
  load_user_profile            = true

  depends_on = [windows_feature.iis]
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Application pool name. 1-64 characters; must not contain `/ \ [ ] : ; , ? * " < > |` and must not have leading or trailing spaces. Immutable after creation (ForceNew).

### Optional

> **NOTE**: [Write-only arguments](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments) are supported in Terraform 1.11 and later.

- `auto_start` (Boolean) Whether the pool starts automatically (`autoStart`).
- `cpu_action` (String) Action when the CPU limit is exceeded. One of `NoAction`, `KillW3wp`, `Throttle`, `ThrottleUnderLoad`.
- `cpu_limit_percent` (Number) CPU limit in whole percent (`cpu.limit`, 0-100; converted ×1000 server-side).
- `enable_32bit_app_on_win64` (Boolean) Whether 32-bit applications run on 64-bit Windows (`enable32BitAppOnWin64`).
- `identity_password_wo` (String, Sensitive, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) Write-only password for a `SpecificUser` identity (TPF WriteOnly). Sent to the host on stdin — never in the script body, state or logs — and re-sent only when `identity_password_wo_version` changes. Required when `identity_type = "SpecificUser"`. The value must not contain carriage return or line feed characters (rejected at plan time): secrets are read with `ReadLine()`, so anything from the first line break on would be silently truncated. If the value comes from `file()`, wrap it with `trimspace()` to strip the trailing newline.
- `identity_password_wo_version` (Number) Monotonically increasing version counter for the `SpecificUser` password. When this value changes between plan and apply, the provider re-sends `identity_password_wo` to IIS. Conventionally starts at 1. Must be a positive integer if set.
- `identity_type` (String) Pool identity (`processModel.identityType`). One of `ApplicationPoolIdentity`, `LocalSystem`, `LocalService`, `NetworkService`, `SpecificUser`. `LocalSystem` runs with full machine privileges: plan warns. `SpecificUser` additionally requires `identity_username` and `identity_password_wo`.
- `identity_username` (String) Account for a `SpecificUser` identity (`processModel.userName`, e.g. `CONTOSO\svc-web`). Required when `identity_type = "SpecificUser"`; inert otherwise.
- `idle_timeout_action` (String) Action when the idle timeout elapses. One of `Terminate`, `Suspend`.
- `idle_timeout_minutes` (Number) Idle timeout in minutes (`processModel.idleTimeout`, 0-43200; `0` disables the timeout).
- `load_user_profile` (Boolean) Whether IIS loads the user profile for the pool identity (`processModel.loadUserProfile`).
- `managed_pipeline_mode` (String) Managed pipeline mode. One of `Integrated`, `Classic`.
- `managed_runtime_version` (String) CLR version for the pool (`""` means No Managed Code, `v2.0`, `v4.0`).
- `max_processes` (Number) Maximum worker processes (`processModel.maxProcesses`, 0-2147483647; `0` is NUMA aware).
- `queue_length` (Number) HTTP.sys request queue length (`queueLength`, 10-65535).
- `rapid_fail_protection` (Boolean) Whether rapid-fail protection is enabled (`failure.rapidFailProtection`).
- `recycling_periodic_restart_minutes` (Number) Periodic restart interval in minutes (`recycling.periodicRestart.time`; `0` disables the interval restart).
- `recycling_private_memory_kb` (Number) Private-memory recycle threshold in kilobytes (`recycling.periodicRestart.privateMemory`).
- `recycling_schedule` (Set of String) Daily recycle schedule (`recycling.periodicRestart.schedule`), each entry `HH:MM:SS` (24h). Null means unmanaged; an empty set clears the schedule (full replace of the collection).
- `start_mode` (String) Pool start mode. One of `OnDemand`, `AlwaysRunning`.
- `state` (String) Runtime state of the pool. One of `Started`, `Stopped`. Enforced only when configured (`Start-WebAppPool` / `Stop-WebAppPool`).
- `timeouts` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Resource identifier. Set to the application pool name.

<a id="nestedatt--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
- `delete` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Setting a timeout for a Delete operation is only applicable if changes are saved into state before the destroy operation occurs.
- `read` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Read operations occur during any refresh or planning operation when refresh is enabled.
- `update` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import an application pool by name. The live settings are adopted into
# state; unconfigured attributes reflect the observed values, and
# recycling_schedule starts unmanaged (null) until declared.
#
# The SpecificUser password cannot be imported: after import, set
# identity_password_wo together with a fresh identity_password_wo_version
# before the next apply when the pool uses a SpecificUser identity.
terraform import windows_iis_app_pool.api 'api'
```
